title: Width scaling: ASPECT_RATIO 64->80 (model_dim 640 at fixed depth=8)
description: Changed ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80, keeping DEPTH=8, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128, and MATRIX_LR=0.06 unchanged. This raises model_dim from 512 to 640 (5 heads) via build_model_config, adding ~20M params (50.3M -> 70.8M total) with no other changes.
reflection: Big win: val_bpb 1.000015 vs round baseline 1.012413, a ~1.23% relative improvement -- by far the largest gain in this cell so far (previous best moves were ~0.1-0.4%). This strongly suggests the model has been undertrained-relative-to-capacity in the wrong direction: extra width per token is worth far more than the ~15% fewer optimizer steps it costs (685 steps here vs baseline's ~800), directly contradicting the depth=6 'more steps is better' hypothesis five other agents converged on this round. Peak VRAM rose from 44.0GB to 55.4GB (still well under the ~79GB ceiling), MFU held at 41.2% (actually higher than baseline's ~37%), so there's clear headroom to push width further (ASPECT_RATIO=96 or higher) or combine with depth increases next round. This should become the new baseline, and the natural next experiment is bracketing width further (try 96, 112) rather than revisiting depth=6, which now looks like the wrong direction entirely for this budget.
